source: Spektrum Deutsch A1+, Übersicht zu den Strukturen, printed pp. 268–269 (PDF pp. 270–271)
scope: Selected uses in the book's preposition summary, not every meaning of each preposition. Explanations, examples, and translations are newly written for this reference.

uses: Der Film beginnt um acht Uhr.
The film starts at eight o’clock.
Use for days and parts of the day.
Wir lernen am Dienstag und am Abend.
We study on Tuesday and in the evening.
We are going to the lake.
A position at or by something.
The chair is by the window.
Use for months, seasons, and the expression im Moment.
I have time off in summer.
Going into a place, or to a country with an article.
Being or doing something inside a place.
I am reading in the kitchen.
Vor dem Kurs trinke ich Tee.
I drink tea before the class.
A position in front of something.
Das Fahrrad steht vor dem Haus.
The bicycle is in front of the house.
Use with cities and countries without an article; also nach Hause.
Tomorrow we are going to Vienna.
Ich komme zwischen zwei und drei Uhr.
I will come between two and three o’clock.
Die Lampe steht zwischen dem Bett und dem Schrank.
The lamp is between the bed and the wardrobe.
The starting point of a time range; bis gives its end.
Ich arbeite von neun bis fünf Uhr.
I work from nine to five.
Das ist die Tasche von meiner Schwester.
The endpoint of a time range, often paired with von. Clock times do not visibly show the case.
Der Kurs dauert von zehn bis zwölf Uhr.
The class runs from ten until twelve o’clock.
Something began in the past and is still true; German uses the present tense here.
Ich wohne seit einem Jahr in Bonn.
I have been living in Bonn for a year.
Wir fahren auf die Insel Rügen.
We are going to the island of Rügen.
Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
The book is on the table.
Meine Freundin kommt aus der Türkei.

prepositions.contraction: zu dem → zum · zu der → zur
uses: A destination such as work or the station. Direction does not automatically mean accusative: zu takes dative.
I am walking to the station.
Heute bin ich bei meinem Bruder.
Today I am at my brother’s place.
Die Tasche liegt hinter dem Stuhl.
The bag is behind the chair.
Das Bett steht neben dem Fenster.
The bed is next to the window.
Das Bild hängt über dem Sofa.
The picture is hanging above the sofa.
Die Schuhe stehen unter dem Bett.
The shoes are under the bed.
Say which means of transport you use.
Sie fährt mit dem Bus zur Arbeit.
She goes to work by bus.
für + Akkusativ · intended use or relation
Ich kaufe eine Fahrkarte für den Bus.
I am buying a ticket for the bus.
A remedy for a health complaint.
I need something for a sore throat.
Say what is not included or what you do not have with you.
